docs.text: Bidirectional Promoters in Pediatric Brain Tumors Authors: Amirfaham Fallahpour , Farnoosh Abbas Aghababazadeh , Kevin Wang Contact: bhklab.amirfahamfallahpour@gmail.com , amirfaham.fallahpour@uhn.ca Description: A pan-brain screen of bidirectional promoters in pediatric brain tumors: which shared promoters are altered (methylation, copy number, mutation) and how each change affects both partner genes, including microRNAs. Project Overview A bidirectional promoter is a short stretch of DNA between two genes on opposite strands that start transcription away from each other. One promoter controls two genes, so a single change there (for example, DNA methylation) can affect both. One partner can be a protein-coding gene and the other a non-coding RNA such as a microRNA. This project screens bidirectional promoters across common pediatric brain tumors and asks: Which bidirectional promoters are altered in pediatric brain tumors, and is each partner gene silenced or overexpressed? Are these changes specific to one tumor type, or shared across types? Do they differ by molecular subtype, and are they linked to survival? Cohort: Children's Brain Tumor Network (CBTN) tumors with whole-genome sequencing, RNA-seq, DNA methylation and microRNA data. We start with six tumor types (low-grade glioma, ependymoma, medulloblastoma, ganglioglioma, high-grade glioma and adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma) and then extend to adult datasets. Approach: Gene pairs: build the list of bidirectional gene pairs from GENCODE v39, the version CBTN uses Curation: standardize clinical and molecular data into a MultiAssayExperiment , following the ICB_Common curation standard and ONCOTREE tumor names Screen: test each promoter alteration against the expression of both partner genes, compared with single-direction promoters Context: compare results across tumor types and molecular subtypes, and with overall survival Set Up Prerequisites Pixi is required to run this project. If you haven't installed it yet, follow these instructions Installation # Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/wanglab-cns/bidirectional-promoters.git cd bidirectional-promoters # Install dependencies via Pixi pixi install Repository Structure bidirectional-promoters/ ├── config/ # Configuration files (dataset versions, cutoffs) ├── data/ # Not shared on GitHub; README in each folder │ ├── rawdata/ # Downloaded data, never edited │ ├── procdata/ # Curated and processed data │ └── results/ # Analysis outputs ├── docs/ # Project documentation (MkDocs) │ ├── README.md # This page │ ├── data_sources.md # Every dataset: source, version, access date, citation │ ├── usage.md # How to set up and run the analysis │ └── devnotes.md # Dated design decisions ├── metadata/ # Dataset descriptions and mapping tables ├── workflow/ │ ├── notebooks/ # Exploration notebooks │ └── scripts/ # Curation and analysis scripts, numbered in run order └── pixi.toml # Pixi environment Data No data is stored in this repository, only code and documentation. Every dataset is listed in docs/data_sources.md with its source, version, access date and citation. docs.text: Developer Notes Purpose of This Section This section is for documenting technical decisions, challenges, and solutions encountered during your project. These notes are valuable for: Future you (who will forget why certain decisions were made) Collaborators who join the project later People coming from your publication who want to reproduce your work Anyone who might want to extend your research What to Document Design Decisions Document important decisions about your project's architecture, algorithms, or methodologies: ## Choice of RNA-Seq Analysis Pipeline [2025-04-25] We chose the kallisto over STAR pipeline for the following reasons: 1. The CCLE dataset is very large, and kallisto is faster for quantifying large datasets 2. GDSC used kallisto, so we can compare our results with theirs Technical Challenges Record significant problems you encountered and how you solved them ## Sample Name Format Issue [2025-04-25] We encountered a problem with sample name formats between the CCLE and GDSC datasets. The CCLE dataset uses "BRCA-XX-XXXX" format, while the GDSC dataset uses "BRCA-XX-XXXX-XX". We had to write a script to remove the last two characters from the sample names in the GDSC dataset. docs.text: No HTG EdgeSeq normal brain, pediatric or adult. No public normal optic nerve methylation. CTRL_OPTIC is only in the Heidelberg set, behind a DTA. No postnatal spinal cord methylation on 450K or EPIC; only fetal (GSE69502). Spinal cord RNA and miRNA come only from adults (GTEx). Pediatric pons, hypothalamus and pituitary have only 1–3 samples each (GSE215240 EPIC; GSE244124 RNA). There is no pediatric pons, hypothalamus or pituitary miRNA. No healthy pediatric multi-region EPIC atlas. PsychENCODE is the closest, but it is 450K and has no pons or hypothalamus. Capper control ages are not public. Most pediatric normals are autopsy tissue from tumor patients (CBTN, GSE244124) or FFPE surgical tissue (GSE215240, Capper). Two datasets I could not get: Saratsis 2014 (7 pediatric brainstem, 450K) was never deposited. Mosella 2021's in-house pituitaries have a placeholder accession. Ask the authors for both.

docs.text: Mixing 450K and EPIC: keep the shared probes, process everything from IDATs with one pipeline, and include platform and FFPE/frozen as covariates. Do not mix beta files from different pipelines. Region matters more than age for most promoters, and both matter in infants. Check neuron/glia proportion (e.g. with sorted references such as Loyfer 2023 or GSE289184) before calling a promoter hyper- or hypomethylated. RNA: GTEx v10 and our tumors share GENCODE v39. GTEx gene counts are from RNA-SeQC, not RSEM, so compare at TPM level or requantify.

docs.text: Usage Guide Project Configuration 1. Set up the environment pixi install pixi.toml sets the folder paths as environment variables ( $RAWDATA , $PROCDATA , $RESULTS , $SCRIPTS , $CONFIG , $METADATA ), so scripts never use hard-coded paths. 2. Add raw data Download each dataset into its own folder under data/rawdata/ , for example data/rawdata/openpedcan_v15/ . Add an entry for it in data_sources.md : source, version, access date, citation. Never edit files in data/rawdata/ . Anything derived from them goes in data/procdata/ . CBTN patient-level data must stay local. The data/ folder is in .gitignore , and only its README files are tracked. 3. Configuration Dataset versions and analysis cutoffs (for example, the maximum distance between the two transcription start sites of a bidirectional pair) go in config/ , not inside scripts. Running Your Analysis Scripts live in workflow/scripts/ , numbered in the order they run. Each step will also get a pixi task, so the whole workflow can be run with pixi run <task> . The steps are: Build the bidirectional gene pair list from GENCODE v39 Curate clinical data (ICB_Common standard, ONCOTREE names) Curate molecular data (WGS, RNA-seq, methylation, microRNA) and build the MultiAssayExperiment Screen promoter alterations against the expression of both partner genes Compare by tumor type, subtype and survival Commands for each step will be added here as the scripts are committed.
